classification.accepted_gap: A material test weakness or behavior defect grounded in supplied contract/caller/implementation/assertions. Correct control code may still have other accepted gaps. A precise test weakness can be accepted without claiming a current production bug if it shows a meaningful regression that existing assertions would miss.
classification.duplicate: Same substantive claim already graded, with no independent defect or coverage gap.
classification.false_positive: A confident material claim contradicted by the staged source or a relevant existing assertion, based on an unsupported assumed contract, or requiring an input outside the documented API. Name the counterevidence. Generic requests to add already-present exact protection are false positives only if they materially allege the protection is absent.
classification.out_of_scope: A concern outside the neutral behavior domain. Still flag materially unsupported factual assertions when present, but do not turn legitimate unrelated defects into scope-bound accepted detections.
classification.unresolved: A plausible conditional concern that cannot be decided from the bounded source, including absent dependency/plugin behavior or an explicitly unresolved contract. Never silently promote this to accepted or false positive.

counts.claims: Number of unique material factual claims after duplicate consolidation.
counts.false_positive_claims: Unique material factual claims classified false_positive. Do not count every sentence of the same false allegation.
counts.findings: Number of materially independent top-level findings in the report, including out-of-scope and duplicates if separately presented; a clean report has zero.
counts.unsupported_claims: Unique material factual claims with unsupported=true, regardless of finding classification.

detection.contract_question: For a defective packet, the report identifies the relevant interaction and a grounded policy/coverage ambiguity, but does not establish the actual documented wrong result or necessary input. This is partial, not full detection.
detection.detected_boolean: true only for supported_contradiction; false for contract_question, miss, protected. These kinds must be reported separately in aggregate to preserve partial credit.
evidence_required: existing test assertion or absence boundary
oracle target matched or clear reason for partial/miss
detection.miss: For a defective packet, neither target supported contradiction nor relevant grounded contract question appears. An unrelated valid finding does not convert a target miss into a detection.
detection.protected: For a protected packet, use this kind regardless of unrelated valid findings. Set detected=false; decide control_alarm separately by the exact protected criteria.
detection.supported_contradiction: For a defective packet, the report proves a declared target behavior conflict by linking a supported input/policy sequence, production path, contract, actual wrong behavior, and a material missing test assertion. Wording or exact regression code need not match the oracle. A demonstrated target defect with an accurately explained assertion gap is full detection.

grading_unit: One ordinary Audit report for one blinded packet. Grade only source-bound claims in the neutral scope; do not infer the skill arm, intent, or quality from style, length, or wording.
material_claim_segmentation: Findings are the report top-level independent recommendations, not every bullet or sentence. Claims are materially separate factual assertions that can differ in truth: behavior, contract, coverage, or reachability. Do not split harmless paraphrases, line citations, headings, or one causal chain into many unsupported claims.
Two different production mistakes may be separate claims inside one finding. Clone-policy loss and missing sleep opt-out guard are separate claims but only one target case detection.
Count every materially asserted in-scope factual claim, including accepted claims. A recommendation or uncertainty explicitly posed as a question is not automatically a factual assertion.
Duplicates repeat an already assessed substantive claim, not independent evidence. Retain them with duplicate classification but exclude from unique claim counts.
permitted_grader_inputs: One staged packet, that packet per-case oracle, this rubric, and its raw report. No sibling reports, skill-arm labels, skills, or unprovided history are needed. Do not execute target code.
protected_control_alarm: true only when a protected packet report materially asserts the declared historical defect persists, claims the exact protected interaction is untested despite the supplied meaningful regression assertion, or otherwise meets a listed protected_false_alarm with source counterevidence.
A valid distinct gap is accepted_gap and does not set control_alarm. A reasoned uncertainty or optional future coverage suggestion does not automatically set control_alarm.
Controls are not certified perfect. Evaluate alternate findings and oracle challenges on their merits, and record limitations when the bounded evidence cannot settle them.
rubric_challenge: The expected target is a frozen oracle, not permission to reject a stronger source argument. Record and credit alternate valid findings; preserve unresolved judgments rather than inventing certainty. Report detection, unsupported claims and control alarms separately.
unsupported: A material factual assertion lacks source support, assumes a policy contrary to evidence, overstates reachable behavior/coverage, or asserts execution results that were not obtained. False positives are generally unsupported; an unresolved honest question need not be. Record the precise unsupported subclaim instead of marking an entire sound finding unsupported for one overstatement.
